originality.rationale: Known Veronese real-rootedness is excluded from the novelty claim. Inspected Brenti-Welker and Jochemko study fixed-degree/dilation asymptotics and do not imply the coupled N=d=r fixed-rank exponential rates or their sharp prefactors. Mallat-Waldspurger concerns continuous Cauchy wavelets; Durán ordinary Eulerian zeros. Closest published-finding corpus results concern different kernels, finite Fourier problems, lemniscates and volume splines, without dominating the explicit coupled rate. Residual historical priority risk remains.
residual_risks: An older theorem for simultaneous degree/dilation asymptotics of Veronese or Euler-Frobenius polynomials could subsume the quantitative rates.
Numerical evidence examines only small fixed ring indices; larger k not verified computationally, while the analytic proof is fixed-k.
No independent verification of the proof or publication priority has been performed.

value.rationale: The coupled critical-order Cauchy-jet geometry is a natural analytic object. Its exact persistent inner zero annuli (1/4,16/27,729/1024,...) and sharp exponential convergence law quantify otherwise inaccessible singular zero-location scales, not an arbitrary finite slice or a known-table recomputation. The new rates apply to every fixed k and clarify the transition between a finite polygon and an asymptotic continuum.
